newsitem.title: USA: Allen Telecom ends Envirotest deal.
newsitem.headline: Allen Telecom ends Envirotest deal.

text.p: Allen Telecom Inc said late Tuesday that an agreement between its subsidiary and Envirotest Systems Corp has been terminated.
Under the agreement, Envirotest was to have acquired Marta Technologies Inc's centralized emissions-testing program for the Cincinnati region of Ohio.

Allen Telecom said the deal was terminated because of uncertainty of legislative and administrative actions that would determine the program's future direction and economics. In addition, the company said they were were unable to reach agreement on the financial and other terms of the transaction.

It was not immediately clear if the Marta subsidiary continues to pursue an agreement with Envirotest for its Maryland and Jacksonville, Fla., testing programs. Those two programs were part of the deal when it was announced last August.
A company spokesman did not immediately return a telephone call seeking further information.
Meanwhile, Marta has entered into discussions with the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency about reopening its Cincinnati program.
"Marta will continue to operate its programs and fulfill its contractual commitments," Allen President and Chief Executive Robert Paul said in a statement.

"This does not change our stated strategy of focusing our future on the wireless telecommunications industry, but for as long as we own these emission testing programs, we owe it to the states as well as to our shareholders to run them as effectively as possible."
